narrative.northStar: The ETH / Birkhäuser Scientific Monograph & Technical Atlas
narrative.overview:
Federated Computing Lab rejects the category default of pitch-black SaaS dashboards and glowing neon cards in favor of the tactile, high-contrast authority of a Swiss polytechnic engineering folio and scientific atlas. Every screen behaves like a calibrated figure plate printed on warm technical vellum (#F5F2EB) and cream drafting stock (#FAF8F3), structured by exposed 1px obsidian hairlines (#121316) and subtle stone rules (#D5CFC2).

Because the product's core scientific contribution is anchoring a multi-node Federated Learning simulator to a single physical wall-meter reading (PC1: 0.065 kWh over 190 min = 20.53 W) while modeling cluster-wide latency, active/idle power, and carbon intensity across PC2–PC4, the visual system treats provenance as structural architecture.
keyCharacteristics: Exposed 1px architectural hairline grids (#121316 outer plate frames, #D5CFC2 internal subdivisions) instead of soft floating cards.

Strict typographic tri-voice separation: Schibsted Grotesk for structural headings and controls, STIX Two Text for governing physical equations, and JetBrains Mono strictly for tabular numbers, seeds, parameters, and stdout logs.
Simultaneous mechanism-and-proof layouts: synchronous active compute bars sit inline with hatched idle straggler-wait tails.
High-contrast quantitative legibility across both live browser sessions (demo_server.py) and standalone offline single-file archives (dashboard.html).

rules.name: The Provenance Polarity Rule
rules.body: Every hardware or telemetry table must visually separate PC1 (Viridian Measured Anchor stamp) from PC2–PC4 (Recessed Stone scenario stamp) so physical measurements and modeled ratios are distinguishable at a glance.

rules.name: The White-Free Series Rule
rules.body: Never plot a data series in white or low-contrast grey on vellum or cream chart stages; all four policies (#D9381E, #1D4ED8, #B45309, #0F766E) maintain high-contrast ink visibility on both interactive SVGs and Matplotlib PNG exports.

rules.name: The Heading Leads First Rule
rules.body: Every h1, h2, and h3 leads its container directly; never place a decorative kicker or eyebrow above a heading. Plate numbers and figure tags sit beside the heading in an inline baseline flex row (head-inline) after the heading element.

rules.name: The Strict Monospace Mandate Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved exclusively for numerical values, units, seeds, file paths, equations, and stdout logs—never as a decorative voice for ordinary prose.

rules.name: The Hairline-Over-Halo Rule
rules.body: Never use zero-offset colored glows, glassmorphism (backdrop-filter), or neobrutalist hard offset shadows (4px 4px 0). Boundaries are drawn with 1px solid drafting lines.

dos: Do place h1, h2, and h3 as the first element of their header group, putting PLATE or FIG. badges beside them in a .head-inline flex row.
Do apply .num (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) and white-space: nowrap to all numeric table cells, parameter inputs, and KPI readouts.
Do preserve the explicit provenance distinction between PC1 (MEASURED WALL METER) and PC2–PC4 (MODELED SCENARIO) across every table and chart.
Do keep run_project.py's make_figures() synchronized with the monograph palette (#FAF8F3 figure ground, #D9381E, #1D4ED8, #B45309, #0F766E) and embed PNG provenance metadata.
donts: Don't place kickers or eyebrows above headings anywhere in the interface.
Don't use generic rounded icon cards, nested card containers, or colored side-border stripes (border-left > 1px).
Don't use training-data default display fonts or apply monospace to body prose.
Don't claim or imply that PC2–PC4 hardware profiles or simulated round CO₂ emissions are physical meter measurements.
